Stanchion is a Run-Time Loadable Extension that uses SQLite's virtual table system. To load an extension from the SQLite CLI, use the `.load` command. Check the documentation of the SQLite bindings you are using to see how to load an extension in your application. Here are some examples for different language bindings: `sqlite3` for Python, `rusqlite` for Rust, `sqlite3` for Ruby, and `go-sqlite3` for Go.

Before loading stanchion (or any extension), you may first need to enable extension loading. Here are some examples for different language bindings: `sqlite3` for Python, `rusqlite` for Rust, and `sqlite3` for Ruby. Some bindings enable extension loading by default (e.g. `go-sqlite3` for Go). For more information, see the SQLite documentation for the C API.

Stanchion is both a persistent and auto extension. It only needs to be loaded by one connection in a process and then it will automatically be loaded by all connections in the same process. Loading it from the other connections anyway is harmless. Connections in other processes connecting to the same SQLite database still need to load stanchion.

The following table shows all stanchion data types. Boolean values are converted to integers when passed through SQLite. This allows them to be used from queries and through the SQLite API, which does not support a dedicated Boolean type. See Differences from SQLite: `BOOLEAN` type for more information about the `BOOLEAN` type.

Let Claude Desktop (or Cline, or any MCP client) work with your Proton Mail, with you in control of what it may do. The server can be set to **read-only** or **drafts** mode, where nothing is sent, moved or deleted. Sending and deleting can be set to wait for your approval: `assisted` mode asks for `confirmed: true`, and `PROTONMAIL_APPROVAL=elicit|require` makes the server ask **you** through the client instead of trusting the model. Every change can be recorded in a hash-chained, tamper-evident audit log. The server talks only to Proton Bridge on `127.0.0.1` and keeps its index on your disk; the mail text the AI model reads goes to the model provider unless the model runs locally (see fully local). The threat model says what is and is not covered. The same tools are also available as a full CLI for scripting, cron and piped automation, with no Claude required. A daily brief of new mail and threads waiting on you can be shown as a notification each morning: see scheduled digest.

> **Know the default:** with `PROTONMAIL_MODE` unset the server runs in `full` mode (sending allowed, no approval), but a **new** `setup-claude-desktop` install writes `PROTONMAIL_MODE=drafts` (Claude can read and write drafts, not send; moves and permanent delete are off in its action list). Re-running setup on an existing install keeps its mode. To allow sending set `PROTONMAIL_MODE=full`; for read-only use `read-only` (see Safety controls). Approval by elicitation depends on the client supporting it; only `require` fails closed.

> **Using Proton Drive too?** See **proton-drive-mcp**, the companion MCP server and CLI for Proton Drive (upload, download, share and manage your encrypted files from Claude). Run both side by side to handle mail and files in one conversation, for example save an attachment from here, then upload it to Drive. More in Related projects.
> **No terminal?** Follow the step-by-step guide instead.

Python port of Heroku PG Extras with several additions and improvements. The goal of this project is to provide powerful insights into the PostgreSQL database for Python apps that are not using the Heroku PostgreSQL plugin.
You can check out this blog post for detailed step by step tutorial on how to optimize PostgreSQL using PG Extras library.
Some of the queries (e.g., `calls` and `outliers`) require pg_stat_statements extension enabled.
The codebase is vanilla Rails, Puma, and—of course—SQLite. Basically the simplest possible setup.
